stem.en: Equal masses of hot, saturated solutions of compounds A and B are cooled from 80 °C to 60 °C. Their solubility curves give these readings, in g per 100 g of water: A falls from 66 to 57, and B falls from 360 to 287. Which solution is likely to deposit more solid?

text.en: Solution A, because A has the lower curve, so its water can hold less.
Both the same, because both cool by 20 °C.
Solution B, because its curve falls more steeply.
Neither, because solid comes out only near room temperature.

explanation.en: Solid comes out when the solubility falls, so compare the falls: B loses 73 g per 100 g of water, and A only 9 g. B's curve is the steeper one. This holds for equal masses too: B gives 73 g from 460 g of solution, A gives 9 g from 166 g. The same cooling does not mean the same solid, and a low curve only means less was dissolved.

hints.en: Subtract to find how far each solubility falls.
Which compound's water can keep much less dissolved after cooling?
